text:
Ava: heads-up — invoice-preview for tenant `acme-42` spiked (~3x) right after the routing-policy rollout at 09:12. chart: https://dash.internal/redwood/invoices/preview/ACME-42 :eyes:
Ken: on it. looking at ingest — I see a lot of events with route_id=null around that time. suspect fallback routing.
Priya: fallback => did requests get retried or duplicated at the edge?
Marcus: quick theory: route-resolver v2 returned header `X-Route-ID` but our proxy still reads `x-route`. mismatched case/name => resolver mismatch + retries = double attribution.
Ava: ugh. that would both misattribute and double-count tokens. can we confirm with raw events?
Ken: snippet from kafka payload: ```{\n  "tenant":"acme-42",\n  "event_type":"token_emit",\n  "route":null,\n  "request_id":"r-123",\n  "retries":1\n}```
Jordan: if route is null downstream aggregator tags it as default-route so invoice preview groups it under default and counts duplicate tokens.
Priya: two problems to solve: 1) short-term reconciliation for invoices, 2) longer-term telemetry to avoid this class of bugs.
Marcus: short term: we can patch the proxy to accept both header names, and add a canary rule to prefer v2 header when present. roll it to canary env for 10% of traffic.
Ava: also need a console signal — add a column to invoice-preview: `route_resolution_version` and `route_source` so ops can filter anomalous spikes by resolution version.
Ken: schema change request: add optional string `route_resolution_version` to billing event proto. will increase event size ~6-12 bytes typical, negligible. backfill: we can populate for new events only, and run reconciliation job for past 24h.
Jordan: caution: adding new proto field requires consumers to be tolerant. aggregator, samplers, costlineage consumers must ignore unknowns. are all consumers proto-safe?
Priya: most are, but billing-export pipeline (legacy) still uses strict deserialization. will need a compatibility shim or feature flag on the consumer.
Marcus: alternative: emit new sidecar meta event `route_resolution_v` to telemetry topic instead of changing core billing proto. pros: non-invasive. cons: more joins in downstream recon.
Ava: I'd prefer a tiny proto field for easy joins in aggregation, but sidecar is safer for rollout. can we do hybrid? field optional now + sidecar for parity until consumers updated.
Ken: hybrid plan seems doable. timeline: proxy patch today -> canary 10% in 1hr, proto optional field merged by EOD, sidecar telemetry in parallel, consumer shims next week.
Marcus: can we also tag events that hit fallback with `fallback_reason=resolver-mismatch` so recon can filter?
Jordan: yes, add `fallback_reason` values for known cases. good for alerting rules too.
Ava: I'll open a runbook update for invoice alerts (link to ticket) and add owners: Ken (ingest), Marcus (proxy), Priya (billing-export). ticket: RB-5239.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: proxy patch canary -> target 10% at 10:25 UTC. CI green. :rocket:
deploy-bot: rollout started for proxy canary (10%).
Ken: can confirm logs show both headers being parsed after patch on canary host. initial traffic looks normal.
Priya: I'll kick off a quick reconcile of preview vs ledger for last 4h and report back if deltas > 2%.
Ava: thank you. please add any console mockups for `route_resolution_version` in #docs later — we want UX before EOD. :thumbsup:
Jordan: quick note for future: we should include deterministic route-hash in events to aid dedupe on retries. low overhead and helps replay protection.
Marcus: agreed. added to backlog item RB-5241.
Ava: tagging oncall for visibility @Marcus (oncall)
Marcus: I'm on it, will monitor invoices and revert routing if spike continues.
Priya: will post the reconcile results in this thread in ~30m.
Ken: thanks all.
Ava: :heart:
